analysis:
I examined every unit and found no security regression.

UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift: the change removes connectionLacksAuthorization (base 38-49). The head comment (head 4-6) says the re-registration trigger now uses the blocked ServingReadiness verdict, so only current evidence counts. The backoff, jitter, idle gating and threshold logic in shouldReconnect and retryInterval (head 26-39) is unchanged.

ServingReadiness.swift: only metadata was supplied. The file_changes excerpt shows:
- a new unconfirmed verdict;
- authorized now also covers a request routed since the latest status;
- an early refusal within statusGraceSeconds (90 s) counts as pending;
- a refusal freshness window.
The header states this is diagnostics plus the re-registration trigger, and that the coordinator owns routing and authorization.

troubleshooting.md: lines 83 and 143 change only operator documentation of these verdicts and the re-registration cadence. No commands or secrets are introduced.

Security relevance:
- Authorization, App Attest leases and routing remain coordinator-side (TB-011, T-053). Provider-local verdicts grant no trust; they only gate a self-initiated re-registration and diagnostics.
- An adversarial provider could already reconnect at will, so a provider-side change cannot widen authorization.
- The main risk is availability (A-018): a mis-scoped unconfirmed or authorized verdict could suppress needed re-registration, and an over-eager blocked verdict could add reconnect churn. The backoff and idle gating bound the churn.
- The removed helper's logic (untrusted/offline status, expired lease, missing legacy path) presumably moved into ServingReadiness.

Not verified, because the source was not supplied:
- the ServingReadiness head implementation;
- ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (the caller of shouldReconnect and setter of unauthorizedSince);
- whether a request routed since the latest status could mask an expired lease or revocation in diagnostics.
Integration should confirm the blocked verdict still covers the expired-lease and no-status cases, and that unauthorizedSince resets correctly.

None of this affects T-053 binding or revocation, since the coordinator remains authoritative.
